subject: Future Tech
title: Delivering CRISPR Into Cells
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Delivering CRISPR Into Cells.

hook.text: CRISPR is useless if it can't reach the right cells. Delivery is the biggest bottleneck in gene therapy today.

buildup.text: Viruses are the most common delivery vehicle. Scientists hollow out harmless viruses and fill them with CRISPR cargo.

discovery.text: Lipid nanoparticles, the same tech behind mRNA vaccines, can also carry CRISPR components into cells without a virus.

twist.text: Most methods work well for the liver because it filters blood. Reaching the brain, muscles, or lungs is far harder.

climax.text: New delivery tech using engineered proteins and cell-penetrating peptides aims to target specific organs precisely.

punchline.text: The editor is ready. The delivery truck is still in traffic.

quiz.question: Why is the liver the easiest organ to target with gene therapy?
